description: Solo team on Field Shift. I'm combining NASA satellite data (MODIS NDVI, NASA POWER) with a low-cost laser NDVI sensor I built, to make crop-health data usable for small farms in Ethiopia. I'm here for hands-on experience and feedback, and I'm looking for teammates in data, software and agriculture for 2027
summary: In summary, the project I did aims to help increase the precision of the satellite data NASA provides. My project's primary focus is in the sub-saharan region where agriculture is primarily done with guesswork leading to inefficient and inadequate crop production.NASA data could help, but a typical Ethiopian plot is only about 50 m × 50 m, so one MODIS pixel blends dozens of farms, soil and paths into a single number. I pulled NASA POWER and MODIS NDVI data for Downsview Park (Toronto) and Ginir (Oromia, Ethiopia) and found that two NASA rainfall datasets disagree by about 50% at the same spot. My idea is to increase the accuracy of the sattellite data form the ground. To do this I built a custom NDVI sensor using red-dot laser, Near infrared dot laser, rasPI pico, silicon pIN photodiodes and an ESP Wroom. Using this sensor I plan to test cluster of farms with similar traits, i.e. I test a single pixel from the cluster and make the corresponding mathimatical changes to the rest of the pixels that cover the farm cluster. With this callibration NASA data becomes precise and usable for small farms in Sub-saharan region.
details:
What I did today: I pulled NASA POWER data for Downsview Park (2020–2024) and found a ~50% disagreement between two NASA rainfall datasets and a summer soil-moisture drop from 0.64 to 0.45. I viewed MODIS NDVI for Toronto and Ginir, Ethiopia, showing one pixel covering many small farms.
Hardware and tools: IR and red lasers, silicon PIN photodiode, Raspberry Pi Pico, ESP32 camera; Python; NASA POWER Data Access Viewer; NASA Worldview.
